transcript.text: micrwave keeps tripping the eletric, not every time but like 1 in 3 when i press start, whole kitchen goes off. had to reset the fuse box 4 times today

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. Do not use the microwave again or keep resetting the breaker: an appliance that intermittently trips the kitchen circuit when Start is pressed needs a qualified microwave engineer to check it. The leading possibilities are a fault in the high-voltage heating system, or a door interlock/monitor switch that is occasionally operating out of sequence. Both can trip an RCD/breaker as cooking starts. Less commonly, the plug lead, socket or kitchen circuit is at fault. 1. With the microwave switched off and unplugged, inspect only the outside: check the door shuts firmly and evenly, and look for a loose, cracked or damaged door catch/hook. Do not remove the casing or try to test/bypass door switches.
2. Note whether the trip is immediate on pressing Start, or happens only once it begins heating. Immediate tripping leans more toward the door-interlock path; tripping as heating starts leans more toward the high-voltage circuit.
3. If there is obvious heat damage, a burnt smell, a damaged plug/lead, or scorch marks at the socket, leave it unplugged and arrange an electrician as well as an appliance engineer.

candidates: High-voltage heating circuit fault, such as magnetron, capacitor/diode or inverter (high)
Door interlock/monitor switch or latch alignment fault (medium)

reading.symptom: Trips the electrics when start is pressed, intermittently

tags.checkGiven: With it unplugged, look at the plastic hooks on the edge of the door and the slots they click into, and check the door shuts cleanly — food

plan: Safety: a supply trip hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
The fault they reported is: "Trips the electrics when start is pressed, intermittently". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
They asked about something unsafe (repeated reset): do not explain how to do it; the fixed safety wording is shown separately. Offer the safe alternative.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
